Heritage walk · Odisha

Heritage walk in Bhubaneswar: Old Town temples, Udayagiri and Dhauli

By @archaeologywala for Talaash Heritage · Updated 15 October 2026

A heritage walk in Bhubaneswar covers the Old Town around the Bindusagar tank, where temples from about the 7th century (Parasuramesvara) to the 11th (Lingaraja) show the whole growth of Kalinga temple architecture. Separate visits take in the Jain caves of Udayagiri and Khandagiri (about 1st century BCE), Ashoka's rock edict at Dhauli and the Odisha State Museum.

We arrange Bhubaneswar heritage walks on request for schools, colleges, companies and private groups, led by an archaeologist or historian, in English or Hindi, with other languages through partners.

Why Bhubaneswar matters for Indian heritage

Few places let you walk through five centuries of one architectural tradition in a single morning. Bhubaneswar's Old Town, known in texts as Ekamra Kshetra, still has dozens of standing stone temples in the Kalinga style, from small early shrines to the towering Lingaraja. Around the city are some of the most important sites of ancient Odisha: Sisupalgarh, a fortified early historic city; Dhauli, where Ashoka's rock edicts address the people of conquered Kalinga; and the Udayagiri caves, where the Hathigumpha inscription records the Jain king Kharavela.

Our programme Bhubaneswar Ekamra: temples and urban sacred landscape is built around exactly this walk, and the Kalinga temple architecture lecture gives the terms (rekha deula, pidha deula, jagamohana) you will use on site.

Historical places in Bhubaneswar by period

The Mauryan layer is at Dhauli, where Ashoka's edicts were cut into a rock face after the Kalinga war in the 3rd century BCE, with a carved elephant above them. The 1st century BCE belongs to Kharavela of the Mahameghavahana dynasty and the Jain monastic caves of Udayagiri and Khandagiri. Sisupalgarh, on the city's eastern edge, was occupied from around the 5th or 4th century BCE to the 4th century CE and is still being studied.

The temple sequence runs from the Parasuramesvara (about 7th century) and Vaital Deula (about 8th century) through the Mukteswara (about 10th century, often called the gem of Odisha architecture) and Rajarani (about 11th century) to the Lingaraja (about 11th century). The Ananta Vasudeva (13th century) is a Vaishnava temple of the Eastern Ganga period.

Places a heritage walk in Bhubaneswar covers

  1. Parasuramesvara Temple About 7th century

    One of the best preserved early Kalinga temples. Compare its tower and hall with later ones.

  2. Vaital Deula About 8th century

    Unusual temple with a wagon-vaulted roof (khakhara form), dedicated to the goddess Chamunda.

  3. Mukteswara Temple About 10th century

    Small, richly carved temple with a free-standing torana gateway.

  4. Siddheswara Temple About 10th to 11th century

    Plain but mature temple beside the Mukteswara, useful for comparison.

  5. Kedara Gauri Temple About 10th to 11th century

    Temple pair near the Mukteswara with a sacred tank.

  6. Rajarani Temple About 11th century

    Temple of reddish-yellow sandstone with clustered miniature towers and fine sculpture of guardians and celestial figures.

  7. Bindusagar tank Medieval

    Large sacred tank at the heart of the Old Town, surrounded by shrines.

  8. Lingaraja Temple About 11th century

    The largest temple in the city. Non-Hindus view it from a platform beside the outer wall.

  9. Ananta Vasudeva Temple 13th century

    Vaishnava temple of the Eastern Ganga period on the bank of the Bindusagar.

  10. Udayagiri caves About 1st century BCE

    Jain monastic caves including the Rani Gumpha and the Hathigumpha inscription of Kharavela.

  11. Khandagiri caves About 1st century BCE, later additions

    Caves on the facing hill with later Jain images and a hilltop temple.

  12. Dhauli 3rd century BCE

    Ashoka's rock edicts with a carved elephant above them. About 8 km south; vehicle needed.

  13. Sisupalgarh About 5th century BCE to 4th century CE

    Fortified early historic city with gateways and a pillared structure. Vehicle needed.

Museums in Bhubaneswar

  • Odisha State Museum. Sculpture, palm-leaf manuscripts, coins and copper plate inscriptions.
  • Museum of Tribal Arts and Artefacts. Tools, ornaments and textiles of Odisha's tribal communities.
  • Regional Museum of Natural History. Natural history galleries, good for younger school groups.

Best time for a walk

October to February. Summers are very hot and humid, and the monsoon brings heavy rain from June to September.

What you see on a heritage walk in Bhubaneswar

Start at the Parasuramesvara to see an early rekha deula with a simple, rectangular jagamohana. Walk to the Mukteswara and its carved torana, the arched gateway, and compare the more developed tower. Then the Siddheswara and the Kedara Gauri, before the Rajarani, a temple with no presiding deity today, named after the reddish-yellow sandstone. End at the Bindusagar tank and the outer wall of the Lingaraja, where a viewing platform lets non-Hindus see the complex, since entry inside is restricted. The reading sculpture session helps groups identify the figures on the walls.

Udayagiri and Khandagiri are a separate half day: climb to the two-storey Rani Gumpha with its carved friezes, and the Hathigumpha, with its long Brahmi inscription; see our programme Udayagiri and Khandagiri caves: Jain heritage. Dhauli is about 8 km south and pairs well with a session on Ashoka and his edicts.

Museums in Bhubaneswar

The Odisha State Museum has a strong palm-leaf manuscript gallery, sculpture from temples across the state, coins and copper plates. The Museum of Tribal Arts and Artefacts shows material culture of Odisha's Adivasi communities. The Regional Museum of Natural History is useful for younger students. A museum gallery study with an archaeologist works well in the State Museum.

Bhubaneswar heritage walk for schools and colleges

The Old Town walk is ideal for schools: the temples are close together, and the sequence makes the development of temple architecture visible. Dhauli connects to Ashoka in the syllabus, and the caves to Jainism and early scripts. Colleges can use two or three days to add Konark and Puri; our Konark Sun Temple programme and the study tour Temples of eastern India cover them. See also heritage sites in Odisha.

Practical advice for groups

Non-Hindus cannot enter the Lingaraja and some other active temples; view the Lingaraja from the platform outside the wall. Most smaller temples in the Old Town are ASI monuments and open to all. Start by 7 am in summer. Udayagiri has steep steps and monkeys; keep food packed away. Check the ASI or museum website for timings before you go.

Questions people ask

What are the main historical places in Bhubaneswar?

The Old Town temples (Parasuramesvara, Vaital Deula, Mukteswara, Rajarani, Lingaraja and Ananta Vasudeva), the Udayagiri and Khandagiri caves, Ashoka's edict at Dhauli, Sisupalgarh and the Odisha State Museum.

Can non-Hindus enter the Lingaraja Temple?

No. Entry is restricted to Hindus. There is a viewing platform beside the outer wall from which visitors can see the main tower and the complex.

What is written at Dhauli?

Dhauli has a set of Ashoka's major rock edicts, including two separate edicts addressed to officials in Kalinga about fair treatment of the people. They are in Prakrit in the Brahmi script.

How many days do school groups need in Bhubaneswar?

One full day covers the Old Town and the caves. Add a day for Dhauli and the State Museum, and another for Konark and Puri if you want the full Odisha temple circuit.

Is Bhubaneswar a UNESCO World Heritage Site?

No. Odisha's UNESCO site is the Konark Sun Temple, inscribed in 1984, about 65 km from Bhubaneswar.
